# 2 Kings Chapter 15 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 235v–237r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2KI_015_page_001.jpg, 2KI_015_page_002.jpg, 2KI_015_page_003.jpg, 2KI_015_page_004.jpg

---

**1** In the twenty-seventh year of King Jeroboam of Israel, Azariah son of Amaziah became king of Judah.

**2** He was sixteen when he took the throne and reigned in Jerusalem for fifty-two years. His mother was Jecholiah of Jerusalem.

**3** He did what was right in the LORD's eyes, following the example of his father Amaziah.

**4** The high places, however, were not torn down. The people still offered sacrifices and burned incense there.

**5** The LORD struck the king with a skin disease, and he remained afflicted until the day he died. He lived in isolation in a separate house, while his son Jotham managed the palace and governed the nation.

**6** Everything else about Azariah's reign is recorded in the court history of the kings of Judah.

**7** Azariah died and was buried with his ancestors in the City of David. His son Jotham succeeded him.

**8** In the thirty-eighth year of King Azariah of Judah, Zechariah son of Jeroboam became king of Israel in Samaria. He lasted six months.

**9** He did what was evil in the LORD's sight, repeating the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had led Israel astray.

**10** Shallum son of Jabesh conspired against him, assassinated him in public, and seized the throne.

**11** The rest of Zechariah's brief reign is recorded in the court history of the kings of Israel.

**12** And so the LORD's word to Jehu was fulfilled: "Your descendants will sit on Israel's throne to the fourth generation." It happened exactly as promised.

**13** Shallum son of Jabesh became king in the thirty-ninth year of King Uzziah of Judah. He ruled in Samaria for one month.

**14** Then Menahem son of Gadi marched from Tirzah to Samaria, struck down Shallum, killed him, and took the throne.

**15** The rest of Shallum's story, including his conspiracy, is recorded in the court history of the kings of Israel.

**16** Menahem then attacked the city of Tiphsah and everyone in it, along with its surrounding territory from Tirzah on, because the city refused to surrender. He captured it — and ripped open every pregnant woman.

**17** In the thirty-ninth year of King Azariah of Judah, Menahem son of Gadi became king of Israel and reigned ten years in Samaria.

**18** He did what was evil in the LORD's sight. Throughout his reign, he never departed from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had led Israel into sin.

**19** King Pul of Assyria invaded the land. Menahem paid him a thousand talents of silver to back his claim to the throne and strengthen his hold on power.

**20** Menahem raised the money by taxing every wealthy man in Israel fifty shekels of silver. The Assyrian king accepted the payment and withdrew from the country.

**21** Everything else about Menahem's reign is recorded in the court history of the kings of Israel.

**22** Menahem died, and his son Pekahiah succeeded him.

**23** In the fiftieth year of King Azariah of Judah, Pekahiah son of Menahem became king of Israel in Samaria. He reigned two years.

**24** He did what was evil in the LORD's sight, continuing the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat.

**25** His own officer, Pekah son of Remaliah, conspired against him with fifty Gileadite fighters and assassinated him in the fortified section of the palace in Samaria — along with Argob and Arieh. Pekah killed him and took the throne.

**26** Everything else about Pekahiah's reign is recorded in the court history of the kings of Israel.

**27** In the fifty-second year of King Azariah of Judah, Pekah son of Remaliah became king of Israel in Samaria. He reigned twenty years.

**28** He did what was evil in the LORD's sight, continuing the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat.

**29** During Pekah's reign, King Tiglath-pileser of Assyria invaded and captured Ijon, Abel-beth-maacah, Janoah, Kedesh, Hazor, Gilead, and the entire region of Galilee — all the territory of Naphtali. He deported the population to Assyria.

**30** Then Hoshea son of Elah conspired against Pekah, assassinated him, and took the throne. This was in the twentieth year of Jotham son of Uzziah.

**31** The rest of Pekah's reign is recorded in the court history of the kings of Israel.

**32** In the second year of King Pekah of Israel, Jotham son of Uzziah became king of Judah.

**33** He was twenty-five when he became king and reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. His mother was Jerusha daughter of Zadok.

**34** He did what was right in the LORD's eyes, following the example of his father Uzziah.

**35** The high places, however, were not removed. The people continued to sacrifice and burn incense there. Jotham built the upper gate of the LORD's temple.

**36** Everything else about Jotham's reign is recorded in the court history of the kings of Judah.

**37** In those days, the LORD began sending King Rezin of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah to attack Judah.

**38** Jotham died and was buried with his ancestors in the City of David. His son Ahaz succeeded him.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**Verse 5 — Azariah's leprosy:** The narrator gives no cause for the king's affliction here — but 2 Chronicles 26:16–21 explains that Uzziah/Azariah entered the temple to burn incense, a priestly prerogative. The result was divine judgment: leprosy, quarantine, and effective removal from the throne. His fifty-two-year reign ends in isolation.

**Verse 10–14 — The accelerating collapse:** Look at the pacing. Zechariah: six months, assassinated. Shallum: one month, assassinated. Menahem: seizes power through bloodshed. The northern kingdom is spiraling. Every throne is a trapdoor.

**Verse 16 — Menahem's atrocity:** The ripping open of pregnant women is one of the most horrifying acts recorded in the Old Testament. The narrator reports it without commentary — the silence is the judgment. This brutality echoes the very crimes that Amos and Hosea denounce.

**Verse 19 — Pul = Tiglath-pileser III:** Assyria has arrived. This is the moment the geopolitical map of the ancient Near East shifts permanently. Menahem purchases his throne by making Israel a vassal state. The fifty-shekel tax on wealthy men is the price of independence surrendered.

**Verse 29 — The Galilee deported:** Tiglath-pileser strips away Israel's northern regions — the same territory Jesus will one day minister in (cf. Isaiah 9:1, "Galilee of the nations"). What begins here as catastrophe, the prophets will reinterpret as the site of future hope.

**Verse 37 — The Syro-Ephraimite crisis:** The alliance of Aram and Israel against Judah sets the stage for Isaiah 7 and the famous Immanuel prophecy. The narrator attributes the crisis to YHWH — even political threats are instruments of divine purpose.

*— PNEUMA*
